classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the initial and reduced velocities, calibrate the supplied exponential model, convert minutes to seconds and calculate the final percentage decrease.

content.prompt: The velocity of a particle is given by $v=100+280e^{-kt}$. If the velocity decreases by $20\%$ after $50$ seconds, find the percentage decrease in velocity after $3$ minutes. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
Initial velocity:
$$\begin{align*}v_0&=100+280\\&=380\end{align*}$$
After $50$ seconds, the velocity has decreased by $20\%$:
$$\begin{align*}v(50)&=0.8\times380\\&=304\end{align*}$$
With $t$ measured in seconds:
$$\begin{align*}304&=100+280e^{-50k}\\204&=280e^{-50k}\\e^{-50k}&=\frac{204}{280}\\&=\frac{51}{70}\\k&=\frac1{50}\ln\left(\frac{70}{51}\right)\end{align*}$$
After $3$ minutes, $t=180$ seconds:
$$\begin{align*}v(180)&=100+280e^{-180k}\\&=100+280\left(\frac{51}{70}\right)^{18/5}\end{align*}$$
Using the exact velocity in the percentage calculation:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage decrease}&=\frac{380-\left[100+280(51/70)^{18/5}\right]}{380}\times100\\&\approx50.1\%.\end{align*}$$
